requirements.promptTitle: Master Prompt — Core Financial Operating System
requirements.title: OWNER SUPER ADMIN
requirements.text:
Create a supreme Group Super Admin / Owner Console.
The Super Admin can:
Create companies.
Archive companies.
Create company groups.
Clone company configurations.
Create branches.
Create departments.
Create users.
Create roles.
Create custom roles.
Assign accountants.
Assign auditors.
Assign finance managers.
Assign department heads.
Control every permission.
View every company.
View consolidated accounts.
Drill from group numbers into individual transactions.
Approve/reject transactions.
Lock accounting periods.
Reopen periods with authorization.
Control integrations.
Control AI permissions.
Control banking access.
Control reports.
Control exports.
Control audit access.
Control sensitive-data visibility.
Impersonate authorized application roles for troubleshooting, with full audit logging.
The Owner Dashboard should provide an immediate financial picture of the entire group.
requirements.evidence: Companies, Team, PeriodClose, Genesis · src/pages/SystemHealth.tsx · src/engine/features.ts capabilityOn · src/store/app.ts · src/App.tsx Need · src/ui/Shell.tsx · src/api/demoPlatform.ts · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql feature_flags, set_feature_flag, integrations, save_integration · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T257 T258 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'capabilities are switched by a Group Super Admin; backups are recorded by a person and never changed' 'the register of integrations holds no secret, and guards what can move money'
requirements.notes: Built: create/archive/clone companies, units, access grants, period lock/reopen, approve/reject, consolidated view, drill-down (Phase 1). Phase 3 adds two controls that only a Group Super Admin holds: capability switches under System Health, by which a module is switched on or off for the whole group, one company, one role, or one company and role (T258) — a switch hides the menu entry and, for the screens built in Phase 3, the screen itself, and it changes no permission; and the register of integrations, in which an integration that can move money is made active only by a Group Super Admin, after a recorded test in a sandbox (T257). Not built: custom-role editor; impersonation; control of integrations beyond the register (no system is connected: the register records intent and controls no connection); control of AI permissions (the switches named NUMI and Voice commands are read by no screen, so Ask NUMI stays in the header when they are off); control of exports; a switch does not close a screen of Phase 1 or 2 to a person who opens it by its address, because those routes do not read the switch.

requirements.notes: Built: 27 field types can be defined and versioned in Genesis (Phase 1), for the whole group or for one company, mandatory or optional, and limited to a sub-type where wanted (a register kind, a document type, a party type), in which case a required field is asked only of records of that sub-type (T150, T151, T154); values are stored against defined fields only and required fields are enforced by the database (T127, T128); a field defined for invoices and bills, register items, fixed assets or parties appears on those records under 'Additional information' (for a party, on its Operations tab), where its value is entered and saved, with inputs for text, number, money, percentage, date, yes/no and a choice from options. requirements.notes: Built: a Group Super Admin can define a new kind of record (a register kind) with its own fields, reference prefix, category and optional cost-tracking dimension. Records of that kind can be created, edited, searched, given documents and follow-ups, and they appear in Forward. T70–T73 test the register engine on the supplied kinds. Phase 3 adds, beside the kinds and not as part of them: a workflow designed in the Scenario Studio — a straight line of steps, a form, approval steps that the person who started the case cannot complete, documents required per step — whose steps may point to a register item, so that a record of a custom kind can be the subject of a case (T247, T249 and T251 test the workflow engine, not a custom kind). requirements.notes: Built: double entry, journals, contra, receipts, payments, purchases, sales, notes, cash/bank book, day book, TB, P&L, BS, cash flow, control accounts, advances, loans, intercompany, suspense (Phase 1, tested). Phase 2 adds depreciation by straight-line or written-down value, calculated for a month when a person starts the run and posted on approval (T30–T38); asset disposal (T39–T41) and impairment; loan disbursement and instalments (T84–T90); fixed deposit placement and closure (T91–T93); entries for advances, expense claims, fund transfers and payroll. requirements.notes: A person with scenario.view builds a scenario on the Digital Twin screen; saving needs scenario.manage (tested, T242). The five examples exist as assumptions: revenue changes, operating expenses change, customers pay later, an asset is bought, interest rates change. A scenario is saved as Base, Optimistic, Conservative or Custom, and the lab derives an optimistic and a conservative case from the assumptions typed; in them a longer delay in paying suppliers counts as helping cash (tested). Every result, table, chart and export carries the word SIMULATION; a saved run cannot be relabelled (tested, T245) and saving touches no entry (tested, T244). The status is IMPLEMENTED and not TESTED because the effect of 'expenses rise 15%' and of 'interest rates rise' has no test of its own. The questions are built with controls on the screen. Asked in words to NUMI, three of the five examples are read: 'revenue drops 20%', 'expenses rise 15%' and 'collections are delayed 30 days' (tested: 'collections are delayed 30 days' in these words, and a fall in revenue in the words 'revenue falls by 20%'; the reading of a rise in expenses has no test). 'We purchase 5 crore of equipment' is not read, because NUMI reads no purchase of an asset, and 'interest rates rise' is not read without a figure: asked alone, NUMI says that it could not read an assumption; asked beside an assumption it reads, it names the part it could not read and says that it is not in the result (tested). Which way a figure points is read in the part of the sentence the figure stands in, not in the whole question: a fall of sales in one part does not lower the interest rates of another (tested). A number of days is read as later or as sooner where the words say so; where they say neither it is not read and is named as not read (tested).

requirements.promptTitle: Master Prompt — Core Financial Operating System
requirements.title: THE ULTIMATE GOAL
requirements.text:
GHL NUMERO should answer one fundamental question:
Where is every rupee, where did it come from, where did it go, why did it move, who authorized it, what document supports it, what does it affect, and what requires attention next?
Whether the Owner controls:
5 companies,
50 companies,
500 companies,
or businesses in completely different industries,
GHL NUMERO should remain one coherent financial operating system.
The Owner sees the entire financial universe.
The CFO sees financial control.
The accountant sees accurate books.
The department head sees their budget.
The auditor sees evidence.
The employee sees only what they need.
And NUMERO AI sits across the authorized system, converting complex accounting data into understandable, evidence-backed financial intelligence.
FINAL BUILD DIRECTIVE
Do not create a superficial dashboard prototype.
Design the database, accounting engine, tenant architecture, permissions, posting engine, audit trail and configuration framework FIRST.
Then build the interface around those foundations.
Every transaction must be traceable.
Every posted accounting entry must balance.
Every sensitive action must be attributable.
Every company must remain logically isolated.
Every consolidated figure must drill down to its source.
Every AI conclusion must distinguish facts from suggestions.
Every automated action must respect authorization.
Every module must be configurable.
Every industry-specific feature must plug into the same accounting core.
Build GHL NUMERO as if it will eventually manage hundreds of companies, billions in transactions, multiple jurisdictions, thousands of employees and decades of financial history.
This is not another accounting package.
This is the financial nervous system of the entire GHL ecosystem.

Credit Bank ₹10,00,000

Who received it?
Which company paid it?
Which office initiated it?
Who requested it?
Who approved it?
Which vendor?
Which contract?
Which invoice?
Which purchase order?
Which project?
Which cost centre?
Which department?
What tax applies?
Was an advance already paid?
Is retention applicable?
Was this within budget?
Is any amount still outstanding?
When was it due?
Was it late?

Is the transaction unusual relative to factual historical patterns?

That is the standard.

requirements.notes: Rent, lease, insurance, subscription, service or AMC contract, utility and retainer are register kinds with an amount and a frequency; loan instalments come from the loan schedule. Internet has no kind of its own and is recorded as a utility or a subscription. Forward and the 360 page of the item list each coming occurrence. This is a projection from what a person recorded, not a statistical forecast. In Forward an occurrence is left out when a purchase bill (for money going out) or a sales invoice (for money coming in) from the same party is recorded within half a period of its date — a debit note or a credit note stands for nothing —, so that the same money is not counted twice, and the screen lists what was left out (tested); this is an inference from party and date, not a link between the occurrence and the document, and an item without a party is never matched. The page of the item itself still lists every occurrence. requirements.text:
NUMERO should calculate complete activity cost.
Example:
Business trip.
Flight ₹28,000
Hotel ₹24,000
Food ₹8,000
Taxi ₹4,500
Visa ₹7,000
Allowance ₹5,000
TRUE TRIP COST = ₹76,500
Example:
Company Vehicle.
Purchase/Lease
Fuel
Driver
Insurance
Maintenance
Tolls
Parking
Repairs
= TOTAL VEHICLE COST
This principle should apply throughout NUMERO.

requirements.promptTitle: Expenses, Vehicles, Travel, Petty Cash, Everyday Money
requirements.title: NUMERO MICRO-TO-MACRO PRINCIPLE
requirements.text:
NUMERO must understand BOTH:
₹80 cup of tea
AND
₹80 crore investment.
Both belong somewhere.
Both require appropriate accounting treatment.
But controls should be proportionate.
Do not make a ₹100 office purchase require the same workflow as a ₹10 crore transaction.
requirements.evidence: src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/engine/analysis.ts attentionOf, forOwner · src/pages/Control.tsx · src/engine/reality.ts · src/api/demoPlatform.ts · src/api/demoControl.ts · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql attention_rules, attention_class · supabase/migrations/0016_reality_control.sql · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T220 T221 T230 · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T276 T277 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'who attends to what: the rule of the group decides, and the owner is shown only what needs the owner' 'the owner is not told of every approval that waits: only of what the rules class for the owner'
requirements.notes: Built: nothing of this requirement was recorded as built before Phase 3 (approval rules that choose their steps by the amount exist since Phase 1 and are recorded under requirement 42). Phase 3 adds two controls that follow the amount: rules of attention, set by a Group Super Admin under Notifications › Rules, which class a notice or an alert by its kind and its amount as information, finance action, management action, owner action or critical, so that of the approvals that wait the owner is told only of those the rules class for the owner (T276, T277); and a materiality threshold for each company, set with its basis under Control, above which a difference found by a verification, a confirmation or NUMERO Reality is raised as a priority and below which it is left for routine review (T220, T221, T230). Not built: any rule supplied with the application — without a rule of the group nothing is classed as owner action, and where no threshold is recorded for a company every difference counts as above it; the percentage recorded with a threshold is not used in the comparison; a workflow of the Scenario Studio cannot take another path by the amount; proportion in the accounting treatment itself.

requirements.promptTitle: Expenses, Vehicles, Travel, Petty Cash, Everyday Money
requirements.title: FINAL OPERATIONS DIRECTIVE
requirements.text:
GHL NUMERO must become capable of answering:
How much are we spending?
Where?
On what?
For whom?
By whom?
Which company?
Which office?
Which department?
Which project?
Which vehicle?
Which trip?
Which customer?
Which vendor?
Was it budgeted?
Was it approved?
Was it paid?
Was tax handled?
Is there a receipt?
Is an advance unsettled?
Is money recoverable?
Was the expense shared?
What is still committed?
What will become due next?
What does the historical pattern show?
And:
CAN I CLICK THE NUMBER AND SEE THE PROOF?
The answer should always be:
YES.

requirements.evidence: src/numi/engine.ts · src/numi/ops.ts · tests/numiOps.test.ts › the wording of the specification's own example questions · tests/numiOps.test.ts › cash, receivables and approvals answer as before · tests/numiOps.test.ts › whole words only
requirements.notes: Built: each of the 18 example questions was put to NUMI on the sample data on 2026-09-27. Sixteen were answered on their subject, from recorded data: whether we are profitable; the money we actually have; what people owe us; what we owe (supplier bills only); which expenses increased; the cash needed next month (a projection over the next 61 days, labelled FORECAST); payments due this week; which companies consume cash; the profit and loss of the whole group (company figures before intercompany eliminations, and the answer says so); the balance sheet of the whole group; actual against budget (the lines that are over budget); unreconciled transactions (a count of unreconciled bank lines inside the answer on the integrity of the books, not a list); audit exceptions; working capital (a figure inside the answer on the balance sheet); where the money went (total expense by company); why profit moved (the two periods side by side — revenue, gross profit, operating expenses, profit after tax — with no business reason claimed). Not built: 'Which department overspent?' is answered with the budget lines that are over budget, by ledger and company (tested for its subject); budgets are kept by ledger, so nothing compares the spending of a department with a budget; 'Which invoices are overdue?' is answered with the customers who owe the most and the total overdue, not with the overdue invoices; 'Show me where ₹10 crore went' does not follow the amount named.

Current financial position.

Commitments, obligations, expected inflows/outflows and forecasts.

Anomalies, mismatches, control failures and potential fraud.

In Forward an occurrence is left out when a purchase bill (for money going out) or a sales invoice (for money coming in) from the same party is recorded within half a period of its date — a debit note or a credit note stands for nothing —, so the same obligation is not counted twice, and the screen lists what was left out (tested); this is an inference from party and date, not a link to the bill, and an item without a party is never matched. The next due date does not advance by itself: a person moves it, and an occurrence that has passed and has no such bill stays listed as overdue.

requirements.notes: Stock still in the books is listed under near expiry, expired, damaged, obsolete, slow moving, missing and held for inspection, each quantity under one heading only. Exposure is quantity times the cost the item is carried at, marked EXPOSURE and shown beside the loss posted in the period, never added to it. Expiry comes from the dates of the lots; damaged, obsolete, missing and held for inspection are conditions a person notes; slow moving is worked out from the last movement. The tests cover expired, near expiry, damaged, obsolete, held for inspection and slow moving; no test notes a 'missing' condition. Exposure is worked out in the application from the records; the database holds the conditions noted. Near expiry is fixed at 60 days; slow moving is 180 days unless the item sets its own. Stock moved to another location of the company is as old as its receipt: a transfer in is not a receipt and a transfer out is not stock leaving, so a transfer does not restart the period after which stock is called slow moving (tested in the database and in the sample engine). Where a location received nothing from outside, the last receipt of the item and lot anywhere in the company is used. The day is kept per item, lot and location, not per quantity: in a location that also received the item from outside, stock transferred in takes the day of the last such receipt there, which can be later than the day the company received it.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMERO Forward + NUMERO Sentinel
requirements.title: FRAUD & ANOMALY DEFENCE SYSTEM
requirements.text:
Create:
NUMERO SENTINEL
A continuous financial-integrity and anomaly-detection layer.
Sentinel must examine authorized transactional and master data for patterns that may require investigation.
Critical principle:
ANOMALY ≠ FRAUD
NUMERO must never automatically accuse an employee, vendor, customer or other Party of fraud merely because something is unusual.
Use:
ANOMALY
CONTROL EXCEPTION
REVIEW REQUIRED
POTENTIAL DUPLICATE
POTENTIAL CONFLICT
INVESTIGATION
until appropriate humans establish facts.
requirements.evidence: src/pages/Sentinel.tsx · src/api/demoCore.ts runSentinel · supabase/migrations/0004_reporting_sentinel_numi.sql · tests/engine.test.ts 'sentinel raises factual anomalies …' · src/engine/analysis.ts unusualEntries · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/pages/Reality.tsx · src/pages/Case360.tsx · src/api/demoControl.ts · supabase/migrations/0016_reality_control.sql · tests/p3control.test.ts 'an unusual entry is measured against its own ledger and explained, not accused' 'an alert under a case follows the case' · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T224 T226 T228 T232
requirements.notes: Built: Sentinel lists factual patterns found in the books of the selected companies, each with its kind, its attention, its explanation in words, the rule that raised it, the facts recorded with it and links to the records behind it; a person starts the review and closes an item as resolved or as a false positive, with a note; the screen states that an anomaly is an indicator for human review and never a conclusion about a person (phases 1 and 2). Phase 3 added three things the requirement asks for: entries that are unusual for their own ledger, listed with the reason and with the statement that whether they are in order is for a person to say (Analysis › Unusual entries, tested); alerts raised where a physical verification or a confirmation from outside differs from the books (tested, T228, T232); and cases, in which people record what they found, with the statuses investigating, substantiated and unsubstantiated, so that facts are established by people (tested, T224). Not built: a continuous layer — the rules of Sentinel run when a person presses 'Run Sentinel now', some checks run when a record is saved, and the unusual entries are worked out when a person opens the screen and raise no alert; the labels CONTROL EXCEPTION, REVIEW REQUIRED and POTENTIAL CONFLICT as classes of their own (an alert carries a kind, an attention of info, review, priority or critical, and a status); most of the patterns of requirements 740 to 764 have no rule.

Phase 3 added: for 'what could go wrong', the Digital Twin with its adverse assumptions and its results marked SIMULATION; for 'does anything look wrong', NUMERO Reality, which lists where the records do not agree with each other, and the entries unusual for their ledger; for 'who needs to act', a class on every notice, case and alert (finance, management, owner, critical), notices to the persons who can approve, and an owner on each case. requirements.evidence: src/pages/Communications.tsx · src/api/demoPlatform.ts prepareCommunication markCommunication · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql · src/voice/commands.ts SENSITIVE · src/numi/engine.ts · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T255 T256 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'NUMERO prepares a communication; a person sends it; what was sent cannot be rewritten' · tests/p3app.test.ts 'commands on the phase 3 screens'
requirements.notes: Built: nothing of this existed before Phase 3. Phase 3 added the Communications screen: a person who holds the permission prepares a message from a template or by hand — templates are kept, in versions, for invoices, payment reminders, statements of account, receipts, approval requests, reports, confirmations of balance, capital calls and other purposes — fills in its placeholders, reads it as it will be sent, and links it to a party and to one of the open sales invoices of that party; NUMERO keeps the words as prepared and they cannot be changed afterwards; NUMERO sends nothing: a person sends the message outside NUMERO and records how, or that it was not sent (tested, T255, T256). A command to send a message is never carried out: it opens the screen (tested). Not built: NUMI prepares no message — asked to prepare reminders it lists what customers owe, and the message is written on the Communications screen; placeholders are typed by the person, not filled from the books; vendor queries, requests for missing documents and audit responses have no purpose of their own among the templates and are written under 'Other'; a message can be linked to a sales invoice only; one message is prepared at a time; no PDF is attached.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMI — Intelligence & Assistant
requirements.title: NUMI COMMAND EXAMPLES
requirements.text:
The user should eventually be able to say:
"Calculate this week's P&L."
"Explain why profit fell."
"Where can we save?"
"Where might we make more?"
"Show possible fraud/control exceptions."
"Who owes us?"
"Who do we owe?"
"What's due tomorrow?"
"What's coming next month?"
"Prepare payroll."
"Reconcile the bank."
"Find missing receipts."
"Prepare month-end."
"Prepare audit."
"Show all debt."
"Show our investments."
"Find unused subscriptions."
"Show unbilled revenue."
"Find unusual payments."
"Explain this contract."
"Prepare next year's budget."
"Forecast cash."
"Show me what doesn't reconcile."
"Show me what I should worry about."
"What am I missing?"
"I'm stuck."
"Fix what you safely can."
requirements.evidence: src/voice/commands.ts · src/numi/engine.ts · src/numi/ops.ts · src/numi/p3.ts · src/ui/CommandPalette.tsx · tests/commands.test.ts · tests/numiOps.test.ts 'debt: principal outstanding agrees with the loan schedule' 'a projection is labelled FORECAST and INFERENCE, and starts from ACTUAL cash' · tests/p3app.test.ts 'investments: carried amount against cost' 'reality: five counts, stated as facts'
requirements.notes: Built: of the 27 sentences, these are answered from the books by NUMI, or open the screen that answers them: this week's P&L; why profit fell (the lines that moved against the period before); who owes us; who do we owe; what is due tomorrow; what is coming next month; show all debt; find unusual payments and show control exceptions (both reach the open alerts of Sentinel, of every kind); forecast cash (phases 1 and 2). Phase 3 added 'Show our investments', answered with the investments carried in the books (tested), and an answer on what does not reconcile when it is asked as 'Do the records agree with each other?' (tested). Not built: 'Show me what doesn't reconcile', in those words, opens Banking and is not answered by NUMI; 'Prepare payroll', 'Reconcile the bank', 'Prepare audit' and 'Prepare next year's budget' open a screen and prepare nothing; 'Show unbilled revenue' reaches the answer on profit and loss, which is not what was asked; 'Where can we save?', 'Where might we make more?', 'Find missing receipts', 'Prepare month-end', 'Find unused subscriptions', 'Explain this contract', 'Show me what I should worry about', 'What am I missing?', 'I'm stuck' and 'Fix what you safely can' are not understood. NUMI never acts, so nothing is fixed, prepared or reconciled by it.

If NUMI is removed, NUMERO should still function.
If NUMI exists, NUMERO should become dramatically easier to operate.
That is the test.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMI — Intelligence & Assistant
requirements.title: NUMI FINAL PRINCIPLE
requirements.text:
NUMI should be:
THE ASSISTANT WHEN YOU KNOW WHAT YOU WANT.
THE GUIDE WHEN YOU DO NOT KNOW WHAT TO DO.
THE PROCESSOR WHEN THE WORK IS BORING.
THE ANALYST WHEN THE NUMBERS ARE COMPLEX.
THE WATCHER WHEN SOMETHING DOES NOT FIT.
THE FORECASTER WHEN YOU NEED TO LOOK AHEAD.
THE EXPLAINER WHEN ACCOUNTING MAKES NO SENSE.
THE MEMORY WHEN THE ORGANIZATION FORGETS.
THE CONNECTOR WHEN INFORMATION IS SCATTERED.
THE PREPARER BEFORE A HUMAN DECISION.
THE EARLY-WARNING SYSTEM BEFORE A PROBLEM GROWS.
But NUMI must always remain subordinate to:
ACCOUNTING TRUTH
EVIDENCE
AUTHORIZATION
SECURITY
AUDITABILITY
AND HUMAN CONTROL.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMI — Intelligence & Assistant
requirements.title: NUMI'S ULTIMATE QUESTION
requirements.text:
At any point, the Owner should be able to press:
I'M STUCK
and NUMI should understand the current context and answer:
"Here is where you are."
"Here is what the numbers say."
"Here is what is incomplete."
"Here is what looks unusual."
"Here is what is coming."
"Here are your options."
"Here is what I can prepare."
"Here is what I can safely do."
"Here is what requires your approval."
And then help execute the authorized choice.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMI — Intelligence & Assistant
requirements.title: NUMI + NUMERO
requirements.text:
NUMERO is the financial system of record.
NUMI is the intelligence operating across it.
NUMERO remembers what happened.
NUMI helps explain why.
NUMERO records what exists.
NUMI finds what matters.
NUMERO FORWARD sees what is coming.
NUMI explains its implications.
NUMERO SENTINEL finds anomalies.
NUMI helps investigate them.
NUMERO stores evidence.
NUMI connects it.
NUMERO enforces authority.
NUMI works within it.
GHL NUMERO + NUMI
NUMERO KNOWS EVERY NUMBER.
NUMI HELPS YOU UNDERSTAND WHAT TO DO WITH THEM.
ASK IT.
SHOW IT.
GIVE IT A DOCUMENT.
TELL IT WHAT YOU NEED.
OR JUST PRESS:
I'M STUCK.
NUMI
ASK. UNDERSTAND. SUGGEST. PREPARE. PROCESS. VERIFY. LEARN. ACT WITHIN AUTHORITY.

requirements.evidence: src/pages/Tasks.tsx · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/api/demoPlatform.ts refreshNotifications · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql · src/numi/ops.ts · src/numi/p3.ts · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T240 T254 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'notices: an approval is told to those who can approve, never to the person who made it, and cannot be switched off' 'notices: what falls due is found when a person opens the application, and finding it again adds nothing' · tests/p3app.test.ts 'what waits for the person'
requirements.notes: Built: follow-ups with an owner and a due date, which NUMI lists when asked (Phase 2). Phase 3 added notices that stay in the inbox of a person until they are read: a payment or any other record awaiting their approval, and again when it has waited more than three days; an alert of Sentinel of priority or critical attention; a case given to them; a follow-up due; a register item of eleven kinds falling due; a bank reconciliation left incomplete. Analysis › For the owner sets the open alerts and the unread notices side by side by class, and NUMI lists the unread notices when asked what is waiting (tested). Not built: a list named Open Loops; a memory of NUMI of its own — what is unresolved is read from the records each time; customer promises, audit queries, missing invoices, insurance claims, refunds, vendor disputes and contract renewals raise no notice (an insurance claim, a dispute or a refund due is a register item and is found in the registers and in Forward); a notice that was read does not come back while the matter stays open, except for approvals that wait and bank reconciliations, which are raised again each week; the question 'What have we forgotten?' is not understood (1026).

requirements.evidence: src/engine/forward.ts earlyWarnings · src/pages/Forward.tsx · src/numi/ops.ts · tests/forward.test.ts 'early warnings state facts, rules and assumptions' · tests/numiOps.test.ts 'renewals and expiries come from recorded dates' · src/engine/analysis.ts complianceView · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/api/demoPlatform.ts refreshNotifications · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql · tests/p3control.test.ts 'deadlines across companies' 'notices: what falls due is found when a person opens the application, and finding it again adds nothing' · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T254
requirements.notes: Built: Forward raises early warnings from the dates recorded on register items, documents, deposits and loans, and NUMI answers 'Which renewals are coming up?' from them (Phase 2). Phase 3 added: a notice in the inbox of each person who may read the registers for an item of eleven kinds — compliance (tax), insurance, rent, lease, service contract, subscription, software licence, domain, bank guarantee, letter of credit, loan covenant — whose next due date is within seven days or up to thirty days past; a notice for a follow-up that falls due and for an approval that has waited more than three days; and Analysis › Compliance deadlines, which lists the recorded deadlines across companies as overdue, this week, this month and later (tested). Not built: a memory of NUMI — deadlines are read from the records each time a person opens the application or asks; contracts, audit and projects are not among the kinds that raise a notice; the notice reads the next due date of an item, not its renewal, expiry or end date; the deadline of an employee claim; NUMERO holds no calendar of statutory dates, only what people recorded; nothing is sent outside the application.

requirements.text: Do not bother Owner about ₹200 while a ₹2 crore issue needs attention unless ₹200 indicates an important systemic/control problem.
requirements.evidence: src/engine/analysis.ts attentionOf, forOwner · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/api/demoPlatform.ts · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql · supabase/migrations/0019_corrections_after_assessment.sql · src/pages/Control.tsx · src/numi/p3.ts · tests/p3control.test.ts 'who attends to what: the rule of the group decides, and the owner is shown only what needs the owner' 'the owner is not told of every approval that waits: only of what the rules class for the owner' 'the class of an alert is worked out from its difference where it carries no amount, whichever way it points' · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T276 T277 · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T220 T221
requirements.notes: Built: (Phase 3) every notice, alert and case carries one of five classes — information, finance action, management action, owner action, critical; a Group Super Admin sets rules by kind of notice and amount, so that an approval or an alert reaches the class 'owner action' only from the amount the rule states, and a kind that points to a control problem can be classed for the owner whatever its amount; of an approval that waits, the owner is told only when it is classed owner action or critical, or when nobody else could approve it; Analysis › For the owner shows in full what is classed owner action or critical and keeps the other classes folded, and the Notifications screen shows the owner the unread notices of these two classes first; each company has a materiality threshold that marks a difference as above or below it; NUMI answers 'What is waiting for me?' by class (the rule, the notice to the owner and the threshold are tested). Not built: a judgement that a small amount points to a systemic problem — only a rule written for that kind of notice does it; without a rule no amount plays a part and the class follows the seriousness Sentinel gave the alert; alerts of priority or critical attention are told to every person who watches the company, the owner among them; a rule does not change the class of notices already raised; the other answers of NUMI are not ordered by materiality.

requirements.notes: Built: (Phase 3) a reminder — a request that has waited more than three days for approval raises a further notice, once a week, to each person who could decide it, classed management action, and this notice cannot be switched off; a follow-up that is due within two days or overdue raises a notice to the person it was given to (the follow-up notice is tested; the reminder of an approval has no test). Not built: escalation — nothing passes an unresolved item to the next person; there is no chain of manager, finance, CFO and owner; the three days are fixed in the engine and no rule configures them; the reminder is found when a person opens the application, not at the moment the three days have passed.

requirements.evidence: src/numi/p3.ts · src/numi/engine.ts scopeFrom · src/engine/analysis.ts burnRate · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · tests/p3app.test.ts 'burn rate is an average of what happened, not a forecast' · tests/p3control.test.ts 'burn rate: cash falling is measured, cash rising is said, too little data is refused'
requirements.notes: Built: (Phase 3) the word 'burn' in a question is read as cash burn: NUMI answers with the average fall in cash a month over the last six complete months, the change of each month, the months the cash in hand would last, and the formula; where cash rose it says that the companies are not consuming cash (tested). requirements.evidence: src/api/demoPlatform.ts refreshNotifications, notifyHolders · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql · supabase/migrations/0019_corrections_after_assessment.sql · src/ui/Shell.tsx · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/ui/HomeBeyond.tsx · src/numi/p3.ts · tests/p3control.test.ts 'notices: an approval is told to those who can approve, never to the person who made it, and cannot be switched off' 'notices: what falls due is found when a person opens the application, and finding it again adds nothing' · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T240 T253 T254 · tests/p3app.test.ts 'what waits for the person'
requirements.notes: Built: (Phase 3) without being asked, NUMERO raises a notice to the people it concerns for: an approval that waits, and again when it has waited more than three days; an alert of priority or critical attention (problems, exceptions); a follow-up given to a person, due or overdue; a case given to a person; bank statement lines left unmatched for more than a week; and an item of the registers that falls due within seven days or fell due in the last thirty — compliance, insurance, rent, lease, maintenance contract, subscription, licence, guarantee, letter of credit, covenant (deadlines, upcoming obligations). The bell in the header and the Command Centre show what is unread, and NUMI answers 'What is waiting for me?' by class (tested). Not built: the notices are raised by the notification engine, not by NUMI, and NUMI says nothing until it is asked; opportunities, promises, missing information and changes raise no notice; what falls due is looked for when a person opens the application, so nothing is surfaced to a person who does not open it; nothing is sent outside the application.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMI Companion — Memory, Decisions, Proactive Intelligence
requirements.title: NUMI CONFIDANT TEST
requirements.text:
NUMI protects sensitive authorized context.
It does not gossip across departments.
It does not leak one company's information into another.
It does not expose Black Vault data indirectly.

requirements.evidence: src/pages/Twin.tsx · src/engine/twin.ts · src/numi/p3.ts · tests/p3control.test.ts 'several shocks at once, and a named expense that doubles' · tests/p3app.test.ts 'a simulation leaves the base and the books as they were' 'a what-if is a SIMULATION, says what it assumed, and writes nothing' 'the questions of the specification are read as they are asked' 'what could not be read is said, not dropped' 'a fall of sales says nothing about interest rates' · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T244
requirements.notes: Built: on the Digital Twin screen the three assumptions of the example — sales fall 25%, customers pay 45 days later, an asset is bought — are entered together and the model runs as they are typed (the engine is tested with these three); nothing is written to the books (tested). requirements.evidence: src/numi/p3.ts · src/engine/twin.ts · src/lib/twinData.ts · tests/p3app.test.ts 'a what-if is a SIMULATION, says what it assumed, and writes nothing' 'a what-if it cannot read is not guessed' 'what could not be read is said, not dropped' 'the questions of the specification are read as they are asked'
requirements.notes: Built: (Phase 3) asked 'what if', NUMI runs the model of the Digital Twin and explains: what changed — each assumption with its effect in figures; why — the formula of each effect and the basis of the model; the assumptions made, those of the model and those read from the question, and what it could not read; where cash becomes constrained — the lowest cash and its month, and, where cash falls below zero, the amount that would have to be found (tested). requirements.notes: Physical verification is a tab of NUMERO Reality; it does not carry the name NUMERO VERIFY. A person starts a verification of fixed assets, of the stock of one location, of cash boxes or of documents on file. The sheet is prepared from what the books say; what was found is entered line by line (a result for assets and documents, a quantity for stock, an amount for cash); items left unchecked need a reason; completion raises an alert for each difference and changes nothing in the books. A sheet opened by mistake is cancelled with a reason while it is open: what was entered stays on it, nothing is raised from it, it cannot be opened again, and a completed sheet cannot be cancelled (tested in the database, T275, and in the sample engine, with a sheet of cash). Verification of assets and of cash is tested in the database and in the sample engine (T227 to T230). Preparing, filling and completing a sheet of stock or of documents has no automated test, so the status is IMPLEMENTED and not TESTED. For a document the verification records whether the document on file was located; the file is not examined. What a verification found reaches Reality: for assets through the history of each asset (see 575); for stock, cash and documents through the last completed sheet of each subject and place, which is counted in Reality health where every item on it was looked at or where it found items otherwise than the books say, and is a difference in the second case, measured by the size of what was found short or over (see 1459). A sheet that left items unchecked and found nothing otherwise is counted as neither and is named under what was not looked at. A case opened on a line of a sheet of stock, cash or documents is shown in Reality against the difference of that sheet, which then offers no second case; a case opened on a line of a sheet of assets is not shown against the difference of the asset, whose key names the asset and not the sheet. The engine is tested with sheets of stock, of cash and of documents made up for the test, and in the sample engine with a sheet of cash completed there and read by the loader of Reality. The call that cancels a sheet through the live data layer has no automated test, and the permission on the button (reality.manage) cannot be observed in the sample data.

requirements.evidence: src/engine/features.ts · src/pages/Features.tsx · src/pages/SystemHealth.tsx · tests/p3app.test.ts 'the inventory of capabilities says what is not connected, and every key is its own'
requirements.notes: Built: a list of 53 capabilities in 26 areas, each with what it does, what it does not do, its state (working, partial, recorded only, not connected) and a link to its screen, with search and a filter by state; the count of requirements built, partial and not built per module, read from the requirement ledger. Every top-level screen of the application has an entry. The areas include Accounting, Banking, Treasury, Payroll, People Cost, Expenses, Revenue, Tax, Audit, Assets, Inventory, Parties, Documents, Forward, Sentinel, Reality, Truth, Digital Twin, NUMI, Security and Integrations. The test asserts that every key is unique and that every capability that is not 'working' states its limits. Not built: an area 'Projects' (a project is a tag on entries and has no entry in the list); the list is written by hand in the code — nothing checks it against the screens, the tests or the requirement ledger, and the state of a capability is typed, not derived.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: BEFORE CODING A NEW ADDITIVE PROMPT
requirements.text:
Claude Code must:
Read the new prompt.
Compare it against the existing NUMERO specification.
Identify new requirements.
Identify overlaps.
Identify dependencies.
Identify conflicts.
Update requirement ledger.
Plan additive implementation.
Preserve existing functionality.
Then code.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: DO NOT CODE FROM THE LATEST PROMPT ALONE

This is critical.
NEVER TREAT THE MOST RECENT PROMPT AS THE COMPLETE NUMERO SPECIFICATION.
The complete specification consists of:
ALL ORIGINAL PROMPTS
ALL ADDITIVE PROMPTS
ALL APPROVED CLARIFICATIONS.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive

Instead maintain structured persistent project documentation such as:
NUMERO_MASTER_SPEC.md
NUMERO_REQUIREMENTS.md
NUMERO_ARCHITECTURE.md
NUMERO_DATA_MODEL.md
NUMERO_PERMISSIONS.md
NUMERO_AI_SPEC.md
NUMERO_TEST_MATRIX.md
NUMERO_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md
or equivalent project-controlled documentation.
requirements.evidence: docs/

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: NEVER TRUST MEMORY ALONE
requirements.text:
For important implementation decisions:
Consult the specification files and existing code.
requirements.evidence: docs/NUMERO_MASTER_SPEC.md · docs/NUMERO_SPEC_INDEX.md · docs/requirements.json · scripts/build_requirement_ledger.py · scripts/check_status_part.py · scripts/_assess/STATUS_BRIEF_P3.md · scripts/_assess/P3_CORRECTIONS.md · scripts/extract_migrations.py · supabase/migrations/0014_inventory.sql · supabase/migrations/0019_corrections_after_assessment.sql · src/pages/Inventory.tsx
requirements.notes: Built: the specification is kept in the repository with an index and a ledger of its 1,916 requirements; migrations and screens name the requirement numbers they serve in their headers; the status of a requirement is recorded with evidence, and the check of a status file refuses evidence that names a file that does not exist; the brief for an assessment requires each claim to be verified in the code. A search of src, supabase and tests finds no TODO or FIXME marker. Not built: a record, for each implementation decision, that the specification and the existing code were consulted; nothing in the repository enforces the practice, and no test can show it. The assessment found the migration files behind the database in one place (the refusal of a management fee for days that have not passed, asserted by test T213); the files were then extracted again from what the database holds (scripts/extract_migrations.py) and the refusal is in supabase/migrations/0015_investments_funds.sql. What the assessment found and what was done about each finding is kept in scripts/_assess/P3_CORRECTIONS.md. One correction was written from the text of a file and not from the function as the database held it, named a column that no longer existed, and stopped notices until the database tests found it; the next piece corrected it. Nothing compares the files with the database by itself: a person extracts them.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: TODO IS NOT IMPLEMENTATION
requirements.text: A placeholder, comment, mock button or empty screen does not count as implemented.
requirements.evidence: src/pages/Features.tsx · src/engine/features.ts · src/voice/gateway.ts · src/pages/Genesis.tsx · src/api/demoInventory.ts · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/pages/Control.tsx · src/App.tsx · src/ui/Shell.tsx · src/numi/NumiPanel.tsx · src/pages/Companies.tsx · tests/p3app.test.ts 'a switch governs its screens wherever they are reached from'
requirements.notes: Built: a search of src for TODO, FIXME, 'coming soon', 'not implemented' and 'not yet implemented' finds nothing, and a search for empty click handlers finds none; the screens of Phase 3 state what they do not do — Capabilities lists the limits of each capability and marks as partial those whose limits name parts not built, Reality, Inventory, Reports, Sales & Billing, Investments & Funds and the Genesis Builder among them, and the controls that only record (notification channels other than the application itself, the percentage recorded with a materiality threshold, the triggers of a workflow) say so on the screen; the empty method wfStock, which nothing called, is no longer in src/api/demoInventory.ts. The switch of a capability governs its screens whichever way they are reached — menu, address, command or voice — through a lookup of the screen by its address (the lookup is tested; the gate on the screens is not), and the switches of NUMI and of voice hide the button, the key and the orb that open them. Not built: two things found in the source — the Sarvam speech provider in src/voice/gateway.ts is a placeholder that reports itself not connected and is never chosen, with empty speak and cancel methods; custom fields can be defined in the Genesis Builder for journals, payments, organisation units and companies, and no screen shows or saves their values (the screen marks them 'not yet shown', and the Capabilities list says so). Controls that do nothing: the capabilities ticked in the company wizard are stored with the company and switch no screen on or off, and the wizard does not say so (the switches are set under System Health › Capabilities); with NUMI switched off, the questions and buttons that ask NUMI on the Home screen, the Cockpit, the command palette, a party, a journal and a report are still offered; asking says that NUMI is switched off and opens nothing. No automated test searches the source for placeholders.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: TEST EVERY CRITICAL REQUIREMENT
requirements.text:
Tests should cover applicable:
Accounting
Permissions
Tenant Isolation
Approvals
Reconciliation
Audit
Security
AI Boundaries
Integrations
Migration
Multi-Company
Concurrency
Idempotency
requirements.evidence: tests/sql/engine_invariants.sql T06 T10d T11e T11f T11g T16e · tests/numiOps.test.ts 'reports a refusal as a refusal and does not say whether records exist' · tests/sql/phase3_inventory.sql T168 T187 T189 · tests/sql/phase3_investments.sql T201 T205 T211 · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T223 T235 T238 · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T244 T249 T254 T257 T258 T261 T262 T263 T266 T267 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'the example of the specification: 100 ordered, 100 billed, 82 received, 100 paid — reality does not reconcile' 'notices: what falls due is found when a person opens the application, and finding it again adds nothing' · tests/p3app.test.ts 'stock is refused to a person without the permission, whatever the records hold' 'a list of the live books is read to its end'
requirements.notes: Built: automated tests cover accounting (balance, posting and reversal, since Phase 1), permissions, tenant isolation (a company cannot write into, use the accounts of or open the journals of another, T11e to T11g), approvals, audit (the trail is append-only, T10d), idempotency (a posting repeated returns the same voucher, T06; an invoice approved twice posts once, T16e) and AI boundaries (NUMI reports a refusal as a refusal). Phase 3 adds: integrations — the register holds no secret and guards what can move money (T257); migration — an import is checked before it enters the books, enters as drafts and the earlier trial balance is compared ledger by ledger (T261 to T263); security — every table has row level security and the internal functions cannot be called by a signed-in user (T266, T267); reconciliation — the comparisons of NUMERO Reality (tested); multi-company — a simulation refuses the figures of a company the person may not read (T244); idempotency — finding what falls due again adds no notice (T254), the same days of a management fee cannot be charged twice (T205), the same difference is one case (T223), the same file is not committed twice (T262); every entry posted by the Phase 3 suites balances (T189, T211, T238). Not built: concurrency — no test runs two sessions at the same time (stock awaiting approval on one document is refused on another, T168, one after the other); the live data layer between the screens and the database has no automated test apart from its two list readers; no test drives a screen; integrations are tested as a register only, since none is connected.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: PERFORMANCE
requirements.text:
Do not solve performance problems by silently limiting financial history or hiding records.
Use proper architecture.
requirements.evidence: src/api/paging.ts all, first · src/api/supabaseCore.ts apiPage, rpcAll · src/api/supabaseOps.ts · src/api/supabaseP3.ts · src/pages/InvItem360.tsx · src/pages/InvUnit360.tsx · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/pages/SystemHealth.tsx · src/pages/Imports.tsx · src/pages/Inventory.tsx · src/pages/StockDocEditor.tsx · supabase/migrations/0019_corrections_after_assessment.sql api_row_probe · tests/p3app.test.ts 'page by page, in a complete order, until a page comes back short' 'a list that ends on the edge of a page costs one more request, and loses nothing' 'a list longer than its ceiling is refused, never cut' 'the size of a page is what the API delivers: assumed larger, the list would end early' 'the latest records only: as many as were asked for, and no more' 'a refusal of the database is a refusal, not an empty list' · tests/p3.test.ts 'the movements of one lot are asked for as such, however many the item has'
requirements.notes: Built: the live data layer reads a list through one of two readers. One reads the list to its end, a page at a time, in a complete order (the key of the table is added to the order asked for); a list longer than its ceiling — 20,000 records, and 200,000 for ledger totals, balances of parties, monthly totals and stock on hand — is refused with a message and is not cut; the message advises fewer companies, or a shorter period where the list has one. The other reads a stated number of the latest records: 200 notices, 300 rows of the audit trail unless more are asked for, 2,000 stock movements (5,000 on the page of an item and on the page of a unit, 20,000 of one stock document), 200 imports, 500 backup records, 50 runs of a scenario. Items, lots, stock documents, conditions noted on stock and communications, which were cut at a fixed number before, are read to their end, and so are the payroll runs of a period (getPayrollLines in src/api/supabaseOps.ts). The page of a unit asks for the movements of its own unit. The size of a page is measured once in a session: the application asks the database for 1,001 numbers (public.api_row_probe) and counts what arrives, so that a lower 'Max rows' setting of the project does not end a list early; 1,000 is used where it cannot be measured. The item page, the unit page, the page of a stock document, the notices, the backup records, the list of imports (while no filter by status is chosen) and the entries created by an import say on the screen when only the newest records are listed; the health screen states the numbers and, against the live database, the size of a page as measured; reports of record read the ledger itself. The two readers are tested against a query that answers as the API does (six tests), and the request by unit is tested in the sample engine. Not built: showing a long list page by page or filtering it in the database — a list is read whole into the browser, and where more than 20,000 records of one kind exist the screen shows the refusal and no list: the lists of items, lots, stock documents and invoices take no period, so that one company with more than 20,000 of them cannot open those lists. The form of a landed cost reads up to 20,000 movements of the receipt and does not say when that number is reached. Not tested: that each list of the live data layer goes through a reader with the right key, the measure of a page as the application takes it (apiPage in src/api/supabaseCore.ts), and the sentences on the screens — that code runs only against the live database or in the browser, is type-checked, and no screen has been driven against the live database. A check of the function of the database that the measure calls is written (T278 in tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql); this status does not rest on it and it is not cited as evidence.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: DATA MIGRATION MUST BE REVERSIBLE WHERE PRACTICABLE
requirements.text:
For high-risk migrations:
Backup
Validate
Migrate
Verify
Provide rollback/recovery strategy where technically appropriate.
requirements.evidence: src/pages/Imports.tsx · src/engine/analysis.ts parallelRun · src/api/demoPlatform.ts · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql stage_import, commit_import, discard_import, backup_checks, record_backup_check · src/pages/SystemHealth.tsx · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T260 T261 T262 T263 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'an import is checked before it enters the books, and enters them as drafts' 'the books of the earlier system beside NUMERO: ledger by ledger, and ready only when nothing differs'
requirements.notes: Built: nothing of this requirement was recorded as built before Phase 3. Phase 3 adds, for data brought in from an earlier system under Imports: validate — the file is staged and checked (every row, duplicates, debits against credits, mapping of accounts) and a file that fails a check cannot be committed (T261); migrate — journals and opening balances enter the books as drafts that are approved like any other entry, and the same file is not committed twice (T262); verify — the trial balance of the earlier system is kept beside the books and compared ledger by ledger (T263); a staged file can be discarded with a reason. Backups made by the database provider can be recorded under System Health (T260). Not built: NUMERO makes no backup before an import (it keeps what a person records); a committed file cannot be rolled back as a whole — the database refuses to discard it and says that what was committed is corrected in the books; the migrations of the database schema carry no rollback and move forward only.

requirements.notes: An integration recorded as able to move money is marked HIGH RISK, is refused in production unless the date of a test in a sandbox is recorded, and is made active only by a Group Super Admin (tested in the database and in the demo engine). No integration is connected: the register records intent, and the date of the test is what a person states; NUMERO cannot check that the test took place. NUMERO itself moves no money.

Not built: comparison of the ledger with the code, database, APIs, screens and tests themselves; the outputs MISSING, CONFLICT and UNTESTED; a single command that runs the whole audit.

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: ZERO-OMISSION AUDIT BY MODULE
requirements.text:

requirements.promptTitle: Claude Code Zero-Omission Directive
requirements.title: CLAUDE CODE FINAL INSTRUCTION
requirements.text:
DO NOT BUILD A SMALLER VERSION OF NUMERO THAN THE SPECIFICATION.
DO NOT DECIDE THAT A FEATURE IS UNIMPORTANT.
DO NOT REMOVE REQUIREMENTS TO MAKE DEVELOPMENT EASIER.
DO NOT SUBSTITUTE GENERIC PLACEHOLDERS FOR DETAILED REQUIREMENTS.
DO NOT SILENTLY IGNORE OLD PROMPTS.
DO NOT TREAT THE LATEST PROMPT AS THE WHOLE PRODUCT.
DO NOT CLAIM SOMETHING IS COMPLETE WHEN IT IS NOT.
INSTEAD:
READ EVERYTHING AVAILABLE.
INDEX EVERYTHING.
PRESERVE EVERYTHING.
MAP EVERYTHING.
BUILD ADDITIVELY.
REUSE ARCHITECTURE.
KEEP COMPANIES ISOLATED.
KEEP ACCOUNTING BALANCED.
KEEP HISTORY IMMUTABLE.
KEEP AI PERMISSION-AWARE.
TEST EVERYTHING CRITICAL.
REPORT WHAT REMAINS.
THE NUMERO PROMPT LAW
NOTHING PREVIOUSLY SPECIFIED DISAPPEARS SIMPLY BECAUSE A NEW PROMPT ARRIVES.
Every new prompt expands the universe.
It does not erase the universe behind it.
FINAL CLAUDE CODE PRE-FLIGHT CHECK
Before beginning any substantial NUMERO task, answer internally:
Have I read the relevant master specifications?
Have I checked the existing implementation?
What existing functionality could this change affect?
What new requirements am I adding?
What existing requirements must remain untouched?
Does this work across multiple companies?
Are permissions enforced at the data layer?
Does accounting remain balanced?
Is audit history preserved?
Are actual, forecast, estimate and simulation still separated?
Can NUMI access only what the user may access?
Have I preserved Forward, Sentinel, Truth, Reality, Control and Black Vault requirements?
Have I considered migration and existing data?
Have I added appropriate tests?
Am I silently omitting anything?
If #15 is YES:
STOP.
Identify the omission.
Preserve it.
Then continue.
FINAL DIRECTIVE TO CLAUDE CODE
You are not being asked to reinterpret NUMERO into a smaller product.
You are being asked to BUILD THE SPECIFIED NUMERO UNIVERSE.
The specification is cumulative.
The architecture may evolve.
The implementation may improve.
The code may be refactored.
The UI may become better.
The database may scale.
The AI may become smarter.
But:
THE FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS MUST SURVIVE.
NO SILENT OMISSIONS.
NO SILENT DELETIONS.
NO SILENT SIMPLIFICATIONS.
NO LOST FEATURES.
NO LOST CONTROLS.
NO LOST EDGE CASES.
NO LOST ACCOUNTING INTEGRITY.
NO LOST SECURITY.
NO LOST HISTORY.
NO LOST NUMERO.
When implementation must be phased:
DEFER IT, DOCUMENT IT, TRACK IT.
DO NOT DELETE IT.

Create a universal:

NUMERO must understand that:

≠

requirements.evidence: supabase/migrations/0008_expenses_advances_cash.sql approve_advance, release_advance, return_advance, save_claim, pay_claim, propose_fund_transfer · tests/sql/phase2_flow.sql T46 T47 T64 · src/pages/Control.tsx · supabase/migrations/0016_reality_control.sql wf_reclassification · supabase/migrations/0015_investments_funds.sql · src/pages/Studio.tsx ACTION_META · src/pages/FlowCase360.tsx · src/engine/reality.ts · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T235 · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T250 · tests/p3.test.ts 'a capital call is a request, not money: approving it posts nothing' 'a distribution: entitlement by units, declaration before payment, tax withheld, a second person for each entry' · tests/p3control.test.ts 'a workflow: checked when designed, enforced when run, and it posts nothing' 'an advance: released above what was approved, held past its date, claimed without receipts'
requirements.notes: Built: for an advance the approval, the release of the money, the expense claimed against it, its return and the payment of a claim are separate events, each with its own function, and an advance is not an expense (Phase 2, T46, T47); a fund transfer touches neither income nor expense (T64). Phase 3 adds: a reclassification is an event of its own, a new entry beside the original one, approved by a second person (T235); a capital call approved is a request, not money — approving it posts nothing, and the money received is recorded apart (tested); a dividend or distribution is declared, then paid holder by holder, each by its own approved entry (tested); in the Scenario Studio request, approval, release, evidence, settlement, accounting and reconciliation are kinds of step of their own, and the screen says of each what it is not (approval is not release; evidence is not expense; expense is not settlement); a release step is complete only when it points to the advance that released the money (T250); NUMERO Reality sets approval, release, claims and return of each advance against each other (tested). Not built: one universal engine of money movement and settlement — each kind of record carries its own events in its own code; a workflow records the events and moves nothing; an invoice is settled by its payments as in Phase 1, with no settlement record of its own.

A fund transfer between the company's own bank and cash ledgers is proposed and posted on approval, and states its kind — bank transfer, cash withdrawal, cash deposit, petty cash top-up, card payment, intercompany — so that a physical movement of cash is told apart from a bank transfer; it touches neither income nor expense (T64); between companies it makes one entry in each (T65). requirements.evidence: src/pages/Control.tsx · src/api/demoControl.ts · supabase/migrations/0016_reality_control.sql · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T235 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'a reclassification leaves the original entry as it is and keeps the reason'
requirements.notes: A reclassification never changes the posted line. It proposes a new entry that moves the amount to the other ledger, carrying the party and the units of the original line, and that entry is posted only when a second person approves it. The record keeps the original ledger, the new ledger, the amount and its side, the reason (required), who asked and when, the date, and both entries; the approval is kept on the new entry, and the screen states the accounting effect. Bank, cash, party, tax and intercompany ledgers are refused, and no more than the line carries can be moved (tested, T235). The rule is the same for every role. A reclassification changes the ledger only; the department or project of a posted line is changed by an allocation or by a new entry. An amount can also be moved between ledgers by a hand-written journal, which is approved like any entry and carries its narration, not a reclassification record.

requirements.notes: Phase 3 built the reclassification, and it never changes the posted line: it proposes a new entry that moves the amount to the other ledger, posted only when a second person approves it; the record keeps the original ledger, the new ledger, the amount, the reason, who asked and when, and both entries (tested, T235). A posted entry cannot be edited since Phase 1, so an amount moved by a hand-written journal also leaves the earlier entry in place; such a journal carries its narration and no reclassification record. requirements.evidence: src/ui/kit.tsx Truth · src/ui/p3.tsx Simulated, Estimate, Exposure · src/pages/ReportView.tsx · src/pages/Forward.tsx · src/pages/Budgets.tsx · src/pages/Twin.tsx · src/pages/TwinParts.tsx · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/numi/NumiPanel.tsx · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T245 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'a saved simulation is labelled SIMULATION, touches no entry, and cannot be relabelled'
requirements.notes: Built: the reports of the library are marked ACTUAL and, where a period is not locked, PROVISIONAL (Phase 1); Forward marks its figures FORECAST, and ESTIMATE where dates are expected ones; the budget screen sets BUDGET beside ACTUAL; an answer of NUMI carries its state. Phase 3 adds: on the Digital Twin the base figures are marked ACTUAL, every result, table, chart and export SIMULATION, and a value typed by a person TYPED; a saved simulation cannot be relabelled (T245); on Analysis the year on year is ACTUAL and the burn rate ESTIMATE; on Inventory the value is ACTUAL and stock at stake EXPOSURE. Not built: the states are told apart by the word on the chip, not by colour alone — FORECAST, AI ESTIMATE and SIMULATION share one colour, and the ESTIMATE of Phase 3 shares its colour with COMMITTED and EXPECTED; no test asserts the marks on the screens.

requirements.promptTitle: NUMERO Flow + NUMERO Reports + Voice
requirements.title: REPORT REALITY LINK
requirements.text: Show reconciliation status where relevant.
requirements.evidence: src/engine/reality.ts · src/ui/RealityNote.tsx · src/pages/ReportView.tsx · src/lib/realityData.ts · tests/p3control.test.ts 'a report states the reconciliation of the records it rests on, and of no others' 'the reconciliation of a report is that of its period'
requirements.notes: Built: every report of the library — profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, trial balance, consolidation, financial health, where the money went and where it came from, ageing, cash and bank book, sales and purchase registers — shows under its heading a strip named Reconciliation. It takes, from the differences NUMERO Reality finds in the companies selected, those of the chains the report rests on (REPORT_REALITY; a report of money also takes every record whose cash reality differs) and of the period of the report — for a report as at a day (balance sheet, ageing, consolidation), every record up to that day — and states how many there are, how many of them are above the threshold of their company (where a company concerned has no threshold set, it says that there every difference counts as above it; this sentence has no automated test), the number by chain, the three largest with the case opened on each, what was never looked at, what the person may not read and the companies left out; it says which records it speaks of and that how many records were checked in each reality is shown in NUMERO Reality, for the books as a whole. It opens NUMERO Reality on those differences, chain by chain, and changes no figure of the report. A person without reality.view is told that the status is not shown; where Reality is switched off the strip is not shown. Which differences belong to which report, and to which period, is tested (realityOfReport). Not built: the status as it stood at the end of the period — the records of the period are compared as they stand on the day the report is read, and the strip says so; a record is placed in a period by one date — an order or an invoice by the date of the document, an advance by its release, a bank account by its oldest statement line unmatched (it is shown on every report that ends on or after that date, since the lines may fall in any later period), a stock ledger that does not agree with the books on every report (it stands, and is dated the day of the comparison) — tested; what was never looked at and what the person may not read are said for the books as a whole, not for the period; the strip is not printed and is not in the CSV export; the reports outside the library (Forward, Analysis with its burn rate and year on year, People Cost, Cockpit, Money Map) do not show it. The strip itself has no automated test: the tests cover the choice of differences, and the loader is tested under 1454. It has not been driven against the live database.

requirements.evidence: src/pages/ReportView.tsx · src/ui/RealityNote.tsx · src/engine/reality.ts REPORT_REALITY, realityOfReport, notChecked · src/lib/realityData.ts · tests/p3control.test.ts 'a report states the reconciliation of the records it rests on, and of no others' 'the reconciliation of a report is that of its period'
requirements.notes: Built: a report whose range holds a period that is not locked is marked PROVISIONAL (Phase 1, requirement 401). Phase 3 adds, on every report of the library that rests on records, the strip Reconciliation: it counts, among the records of the period of the report, those that do not agree with their other records — bank accounts with statement lines not matched for more than a week among them, on the reports of money, the balance sheet and the trial balance — says how many are above the threshold of their company, names what was never looked at (bank accounts with no statement imported, cash boxes never counted, assets never verified) and what the person may not read, and says that what was never checked is not counted as agreeing (tested). Not built: a warning of missing data other than what Reality never looked at; stale integration (none is connected); missing documents; incomplete department submission; a judgement of whether the difference could materially affect the report — the strip counts, it does not weigh; the comparison is made as the records stand today; the strip is not printed.

requirements.evidence: src/engine/analysis.ts · src/pages/Analysis.tsx · src/lib/realityData.ts · src/pages/Reality.tsx · src/ui/p3.tsx · src/pages/ReportView.tsx · src/ui/RealityNote.tsx · src/ui/HomeBeyond.tsx · tests/p3control.test.ts 'burn rate: cash falling is measured, cash rising is said, too little data is refused' 'year on year: a year that is not complete is compared as it stands, never scaled up' · tests/p3app.test.ts 'reality names what it may not read, and does not count it as agreeing' 'the twin names what it may not read'
requirements.notes: Where the records are not enough, the screen says so instead of giving a figure: no burn rate from fewer than three months of balances; a part year is marked with its number of months and is not scaled up; a source the person may not read is named and left out of the counts; what was never verified or counted is listed and not counted as agreeing; the unusual-entries screen states how many lines were not examined; figures worked out by a formula are marked ESTIMATE (tested for the burn rate, year on year, Reality and the twin). The reports mark a range with a period that is not locked as PROVISIONAL and state the entries the person is not cleared to see. The reports of the library now carry the reconciliation of the records they rest on (see 1676): it counts among the differences the bank accounts with statement lines unmatched for more than a week, says what was never looked at — bank accounts with no statement imported among it — and what the person may not read, and says that what was never checked is not counted as agreeing; it speaks of the records of the period of the report as they stand on the day it is read, says so, and is not printed. Where a company has no materiality threshold set, the Command Centre, Reality and that strip say that there every difference counts as material, instead of speaking of a threshold that does not exist; these sentences on screens have no automated test. A warning on a report of missing documents or of a stale import belongs to requirement 1677 and is not shown on the reports.

requirements.evidence: src/engine/reality.ts · src/pages/Reality.tsx · src/pages/Advance360.tsx · src/pages/FlowCase360.tsx · tests/p3control.test.ts 'an advance: released above what was approved, held past its date, claimed without receipts' 'an advance with no date set for settling it is reported once it has been held thirty days'
requirements.notes: Built: for every advance released, Reality sets against each other the amount approved, the money released and returned, the expense lines claimed and how many of them carry a receipt, and the amount recognised as expense through approved claims; it reports more released than approved, claims without a receipt, money still held after the expected settlement date or, where no date was set, more than thirty days after the release, and more settled and returned than released (tested for all but the last). Not built: the release and the return are not compared with the bank statement or with a cash count — they are the amounts recorded in NUMERO; actual use is what was claimed and is compared with nothing else; the thirty days are fixed in the engine and cannot be set; a case of a Scenario Studio workflow shows the record of each step as a link and reconciles nothing.

The test asserts that advances produce forward events; it does not assert the unreleased case specifically.

requirements.evidence: src/engine/reality.ts · src/lib/realityData.ts · src/pages/Reality.tsx · src/pages/Case360.tsx · tests/p3control.test.ts 'an advance: released above what was approved, held past its date, claimed without receipts' 'an advance with no date set for settling it is reported once it has been held thirty days' · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T223
requirements.notes: Built: nothing of this requirement was recorded as built before Phase 3 (Sentinel raised alerts on payments and journals, recorded under requirement 40). Phase 3 adds: NUMERO Reality reports, for every advance, more released than approved, claims without receipts, money still held after the date set for settling it or thirty days after the release where no date was set, and more settled and returned than released (tested for all but the last); each is a difference on which a person opens a case, kept until it is closed with its resolution (T223). requirements.evidence: src/pages/Advance360.tsx · src/pages/Expenses.tsx · supabase/migrations/0008_expenses_advances_cash.sql · src/engine/reality.ts · src/pages/Reality.tsx · src/pages/Control.tsx · src/pages/FlowCase360.tsx · tests/sql/phase3_control.sql T235 · tests/p3control.test.ts 'an advance: released above what was approved, held past its date, claimed without receipts'
requirements.notes: Built: for an advance NUMERO knows who holds it, its purpose, what was released and from which ledger, the claims that settled it with their receipts, what was returned and what is still outstanding (Phase 2). Phase 3 adds the question 'is it reconciled?' for advances: NUMERO Reality sets approval, release, claims and return against each other and reports where they differ (tested); a reclassification keeps how an amount was classified before and after, who changed it and why (T235); a case of a workflow records who requested, who approved and who released, step by step. Not built: the twelve questions for money other than advances; 'what was it actually used for' is what was claimed and is compared with nothing else; the release is not matched to the bank statement; 'who is responsible' is the holder of the advance and nothing more.

ACCOUNTABILITY INTO ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY.
CLAUDE CODE ZERO-OMISSION REMINDER
THIS ENTIRE ADDITIVE SPECIFICATION MUST BE ADDED TO THE EXISTING NUMERO REQUIREMENT LEDGER.
DO NOT IMPLEMENT ONLY:
ADVANCES
or
VOICE
or
REPORTS.

If a feature cannot be implemented in the current development phase:

DO NOT FORGET IT.
DO NOT SILENTLY SUBSTITUTE A PLACEHOLDER.

requirements.notes: Built: a Genesis Builder screen for structure levels and units, custom field definitions with versions, party types, tax codes with dated rates, learned rules and controls; register kinds with their own fields; expense and asset categories; the account mapping (Phase 2). requirements.evidence: src/pages/TwinParts.tsx DriversTab · src/pages/Twin.tsx · src/engine/twin.ts · src/api/demoPlatform.ts · supabase/migrations/0017_scenarios_flows.sql · tests/p3control.test.ts 'an approved driver supplies the value; one that is not approved does not' 'an assumption is used only after a second person approves it' 'a driver in use stays in use while its successor awaits approval' 'a driver supplies an assumption only in its own unit' · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T246 T269 · tests/p3app.test.ts 'the twin starts from the books: cash and receivables are those of the balance sheet'
requirements.notes: The assumptions library holds drivers for a company or the group, each with a key, a unit, a value, what it rests on and whether it is recorded or assumed. An assumption of a simulation may name a driver; the value of the driver then replaces the value typed, only if a second person has approved it, and the result says which was used (tested). A driver supplies the value only where it is stated in the unit of the assumption that names it (percentage points take a percentage or a rate); otherwise the value typed is used and a note of the result says why (tested). The row of the assumption on the screen applies the same rule (driverFits of the engine): a driver stated in another unit is listed as 'not used here', the value typed is not dimmed, and the row says that the driver is not used, that the value typed is, and why. The rule is tested in the engine; the screen has no test. The behaviour asserted by T269 is in the database (migration p3_19, now written in the migration file of the repository) and in the demo engine.

requirements.evidence: supabase/migrations/0006_workflow_registers_documents.sql propose_posting, wf_dispatch, register_kinds · numero_private.open_request · src/ui/AccountMapping.tsx · src/pages/Genesis.tsx · src/engine/reports.ts · src/pages/Calculators.tsx · supabase/migrations/0017_scenarios_flows.sql save_flow_def, start_flow_case, complete_flow_step · src/engine/twin.ts · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql notifications, notify_holders, refresh_notifications · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T240 T247 T252
requirements.notes: Built: engines used by many kinds of record exist since Phases 1 and 2 — posting with its dispatcher (one handler per module), approval (rules by kind, company and amount), account mapping, custom fields, register kinds (entities of the group's own, paths among them), documents with their links, permissions, reports; calculators are on one screen. Phase 3 adds a workflow engine (the Scenario Studio: definitions in versions, cases, steps, T247 to T252), a notification engine (notices raised by the engine for approvals, alerts, follow-ups, cases and what falls due, T240), and a scenario engine for simulations (the Digital Twin). Not built: a form engine (the forms of the records are fixed screens; only a workflow has a form); a rule engine beyond approval rules, rules of attention and the fixed rules of Sentinel; a settlement engine (settlement is written for each kind of record); an AI/NUMI metadata engine (NUMI reads patterns written in the code); the workflow engine does not carry the records of NUMERO, which follow their own code.

A SCENARIO
A FORM

requirements.evidence: src/pages/Companies.tsx · src/pages/Genesis.tsx · src/pages/Registers.tsx · src/pages/Expenses.tsx · src/pages/Assets.tsx · src/ui/ApprovalRuleEditor.tsx · src/pages/Studio.tsx · src/pages/FlowDesigner.tsx · src/pages/Twin.tsx · src/pages/Notifications.tsx · src/pages/Communications.tsx · supabase/migrations/0017_scenarios_flows.sql · supabase/migrations/0018_platform.sql save_attention_rule, save_message_template · tests/sql/phase3_platform.sql T242 T247 T248 T276
requirements.notes: Built: without coding, a company, a department, a sub-department, a path (as a register item), a category, a field (shown and filled in on invoices and bills, register items, fixed assets and parties; on other record types it can be defined and is shown nowhere), an approval route (a rule by kind of record, company and amount with its steps by role, added and changed on the Approvals page) (Phase 2). Phase 3 adds: a scenario — a way of working designed in the Scenario Studio, and a simulation saved on the Digital Twin (T242); a form — the form of a workflow, with fields of six kinds (T248); a workflow — a straight line of steps (T247); a rule — a rule of attention by kind of notice and amount (T276); message templates for communications. Not built: a form apart from a workflow, a document type (the 23 kinds are fixed), a status, a rule other than approval rules and rules of attention, a calculator, a report, a dashboard, an automation, a NUMI rule (learned rules can only be disabled), a Sentinel rule (two thresholds only; a threshold tried on the Digital Twin changes nothing), a company template.

A CONFIGURABLE FINANCIAL OPERATING SYSTEM.
